methodological_rigor.justification: Multicenter (8-center) retrospective cohort with clear eligibility (201 initial, 187 analyzed, 334 nodules), standardized Embocept-S + Epirubicin protocol per CIRSE Standards of Practice, mRECIST response assessment at four time points, CTCAE grading, and both per-patient and per-nodule analyses. Strengths include multidisciplinary tumor board involvement, detailed procedure protocol, and logistic regression for predictors. Weaknesses: substantial imbalance between superselective (n=48) and lobar (n=139) groups with no propensity score matching; no centralized/blinded imaging review (single experienced radiologist); heterogeneity in indications across BCLC stages; per-nodule analyses use correlated observations within patients without clustering adjustment; multiplicity across four time points and multiple endpoints handled only by Bonferroni post-hoc. Statistical reporting is adequate but not rigorous.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective multicenter cohort of a locoregional HCC therapy corresponds to Oxford LoE 4 (low-quality cohort). Clinical relevance is high—DSM-TACE is increasingly used in real-world practice, the superselective vs lobar distinction is actionable for interventional radiologists, and the data reinforce CIRSE standards. Safety findings (no grade ≥3 AEs, no procedure-related deaths) provide reassurance for routine use.

reporting_quality.justification: Observational cohort where STROBE applies. Patient selection flowchart is referenced (Figure 1), exclusion criteria are enumerated, outcome definitions (mRECIST, PES, CTCAE) are stated, and limitations are acknowledged. Gaps include no explicit STROBE checklist, some inconsistencies in numerators/denominators across time points (e.g., 136 assessed at 3-6 months out of 187, likely due to censoring but not explained), and no explicit handling of missing follow-up. Data availability is limited—no deposition or code sharing, and only a case report form is mentioned, so data availability score of 2.

novelty_literature.justification: DSM-TACE with EmboCept has been described extensively (HepaStar trial ref 17, Ludwig et al. ref 10, Orlacchio multiple refs 11-13, Haubold ref 9, Schicho ref 8, Mohr ref 16, Giurazza ref 18). Superselective vs lobar TACE comparisons are established for cTACE/DEB-TACE (refs 27, 28, 30). This study's incremental contribution is specifically applying the superselective-vs-lobar lens to DSM-TACE in a large multicenter Italian cohort, extending HepaStar-like data. A meaningful real-world extension but not a first-in-class finding.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript flows well and provides detailed technical/procedural descriptions. However, several sections have awkward phrasing, inconsistent capitalization (e.g., 'efficacy' at start of abstract), and the abstract contains a non-traditional opening summary before the structured abstract. Numbers in Results sometimes differ subtly between text and tables (e.g., 261 vs 268 for lobar nodules). Discussion is thoughtful and appropriately positions findings, but citation density at times obscures the authors' specific contribution.

key_strengths: Large multicenter Italian real-world cohort (187 patients, 334 nodules across 8 centers) with 10-year recruitment window and protocol consistent with CIRSE standards
Both per-patient and per-nodule analyses show a significant superselective advantage at 3-6 months (per-nodule ORR 66.7% vs 31.3%, p=0.0008)
Robust safety profile demonstrated across both approaches with no grade ≥3 AEs or procedure-related deaths
Four-time-point mRECIST follow-up (1, 3-6, 6-9, 9-12 months) captures the decline curve typical of TACE
key_concerns: Substantial allocation imbalance (48 superselective vs 139 lobar) without propensity score matching or multivariable confounder adjustment for the primary comparison
No centralized or blinded imaging review—response assessment by a single experienced radiologist
Per-nodule analyses treat correlated nodules within patients as independent observations without clustering adjustment
Significant dropoff in assessable patients at later time points (187→136→... ) not explained with a flow diagram
Minor numerical inconsistencies between text and tables (e.g., 261 vs 268 lobar nodules)
No data sharing or analytic code; STROBE checklist not explicitly included
chief_reviewer.rationale: Useful real-world multicenter DSM-TACE cohort with a clinically actionable superselective-vs-lobar comparison, but methodological rigor limits it to Tier 3 with minor revisions to add clustering-aware analyses, a flow diagram, and propensity matching or multivariable confounder adjustment.
